planting.note: Root leaf or stem cuttings in gritty, fast-draining succulent mix in full sun to light shade; strong light brings out the rosy edge color on the curled leaf margins.

directions: Raised at Frank Reinelt's Vetterle and Reinelt Nursery in Capitola, California (some references instead credit botanist Harry Butterfield), this Echeveria gibbiflora-type hybrid is a sister seedling to the better-known 'Blue Waves,' sharing its frosted blue coloring but with a more pronounced leaf curl. Thick, powdery blue-green leaves ruffle and curve at the margins and flush pink during cool spring and fall weather, forming a solitary rosette that can widen to roughly 10 inches across with age. Reddish-pink, bell-shaped flowers rise on well-spaced stalks above the foliage in summer. Grow in full sun to light shade in gritty, well-drained soil, water sparingly, and behead and re-root older plants every few years to keep the rosette tight.
